builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
summary: ChainAgent replaces two-stage pipelines that find vulnerabilities in isolation and assemble attack paths afterward with a goal-directed LLM agent that grows an exploit graph, searching backward from unmet preconditions and forward from discovered capabilities. It costs LLM API calls for iterative source-code inspection plus integration of the graph representation and PHP-specific chaining knowledge, with no training or special hardware required. It can fail through missed chains (recall is only 42-45%), false exploit paths requiring manual triage, and limited coverage outside PHP or outside the vulnerability and gadget classes in its empirical study.
rationale: A PHP-focused, API-backed agent for exploit-chain discovery is deployable on constrained infrastructure, but its 42-45% recall and single-baseline comparison require workload-specific validation before production trust.
technique: Goal-directed LLM agent for exploit-chain discovery in PHP

claims.statement: ChainAgent replaces two-stage pipelines that find vulnerabilities in isolation and assemble attack paths afterward with a goal-directed LLM agent that grows an exploit graph, searching backward from unmet preconditions and forward from discovered capabilities. It costs LLM API calls for iterative source-code inspection plus integration of the graph representation and PHP-specific chaining knowledge, with no training or special hardware required. It can fail through missed chains (recall is only 42-45%), false exploit paths requiring manual triage, and limited coverage outside PHP or outside the vulnerability and gadget classes in its empirical study.

ChainAgent recovers up to 4.4 times as many correct goal-reaching dependency edges as Codex on 15 PHP applications across three shared LLM backends, with 42.02-44.63% recall for goal-reaching components.
